reason: README quick start offers a `paddleocr ocr` CLI using small PP-OCRv5 models that run on CPU with a few hundred MB of downloads.
demo: docs/quick_start.en.md / README: install paddlepaddle (CPU) + paddleocr, run `paddleocr ocr -i <image>`
goal: Install the CPU build of PaddlePaddle and PaddleOCR from the repo's documented instructions, and make the `paddleocr ocr -i <image> --save_path <dir>` CLI work on CPU. It must download the default PP-OCRv5 models and run text detection and recognition on a local image containing English text. The output directory must contain the result JSON (with rec_texts) and a visualization image. Put the environment setup in /work/env.sh so that the `paddleocr` command and the python packages are available after sourcing it.
check: Runs the paddleocr OCR CLI on a freshly generated image with known English text and verifies the saved JSON contains the recognized words and a visualization image is written.
